title: Homeostasis
standard_text: Homeostasis keeps the internal environment stable by negative feedback; control of body temperature, blood glucose and water balance by the nervous and endocrine systems. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 10, Quarter 4: Life Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Life Science): feedback and homeostasis, thermoregulation, nerves and hormones, blood glucose and water balance and the kidney. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Stimulus → receptor → control center → effector → response.
key_sub: Negative feedback brings a variable back to its set point.
body_html:
How to think about it

Homeostasis keeps the internal environment stable. A change (stimulus) is detected by receptors; a control center (often the hypothalamus) sends signals by nerves or hormones to effectors, which reverse the change: negative feedback.

Body temperature is controlled by sweating, shivering and changes to skin blood flow. Insulin lowers and glucagon raises blood glucose. ADH controls how much water the kidneys reabsorb, so you make less urine on a hot day when you sweat a lot.

Example

Blood glucose rises after a meal. Which hormone and gland?

detected by the pancreas

beta cells release insulin

Answer: insulin from the pancreas

Example

Filtrate 125 mL/min, urine 1 mL/min. % reabsorbed?

(125 − 1) ÷ 125 × 100

Answer: 99.2%

Common mistakes

  • Saying negative feedback is bad: it is stabilizing.
  • Mixing up glucagon (hormone) with glycogen (store).
  • Thinking ADH makes more urine: it makes less, more concentrated urine.

items.q: What are the parts of a stimulus–response model?

items.q: What is homeostasis?
